With the main board in the middle, the three boards are chained in this order: power board → main board → sensor board. After inspecting the AP2101 with x ray, they found it properly welded and saw no evidence of poor welding. They reported that powering up these two boards caused the positive terminal of the L3 capacitor to become short-circuited to GND.

candidate_task.speaker: client
candidate_task.text: During bring-up of the 3 integrated board samples, power tested correctly on every unit: the 3.3V rail rises to ~3.3V and the ESP32 runs. Native USB, however, is completely nonfunctional across the set. On the PC, none of the boards enumerate in either normal or forced-download mode, and enumeration also fails with the USB-C connector in both orientations. Using the same cable and port, a known-good development board enumerates correctly, which rules out the cable.

execution.observed_behavior: None of the three integrated-board samples enumerated over native USB in normal or forced-download mode, in either USB-C orientation, while a known-good board enumerated with the same cable and port.

candidate_task.speaker: client
candidate_task.text: Tracing the USB nets in KiCad points to what I think is the cause: the USBLC6-2SC6 ESD component U3 has its VBUS pin 5 connected to GND rather than +5V. The D+/D- routing itself appears correct, running from connector pins A6/B6/A7/B7 through U3 to GPIO20 (D+) and GPIO19 (D-).

execution.observed_behavior: KiCad net tracing showed that USBLC6-2SC6 U3 pin 5 was connected to GND instead of the required +5V.

candidate_task.speaker: client
candidate_task.text: To restore ESD protection properly, please correct the symbol: connect pin 5 (VBUS) to +5V, route pin 2 separately to GND instead of tying the two together, and retain the D+/D- pass-through via U3. When USBLC6 is wired correctly, protection returns and USB operates. Is that what you intend to change? There is no rush; I will continue testing meanwhile.
